title: POC Weekly Sync — Retry playbook, fallbacks & escalation
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on last week's spike of 5xx/timeouts during batch jobs. Confirmed root cause likely a combination of aggressive client-side retry loops and an unlucky sequence-length distribution increasing GPU memory pressure. Agreed immediate mitigations: temper client retries, enable per-route prefix cache for stable requests, turn on fallback routing to a smaller model for degraded latency, and run a focused benchmark with telemetry turned up. Redwood to share a runbook and tuned retry template; Nimbus to run canary with 10% traffic and report metrics mid-week.
topics: Retry policy interaction with rate limits
Fallback routing to smaller quantized model
Canary rollout plan and escalation path
Telemetry gaps and log correlation IDs

Nimbus to run canary at 10% traffic for 48h starting 2026-04-14 and share latency/5xx sheets
Redwood SE to enable debug telemetry and share link to traces for failing requests
Schedule follow-up deep-dive with network team if errors persist (TBD)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM); Dana Miller (Nimbus CTO), Jamal Khan (Principal Eng), Lena Ortiz (SRE), Marisol (PM)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
- 5xx spike during batch window last Wed; pattern of 502/504; retries amplified load.
- Need to marry client retry config with server-side rate limits and backpressure.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're on for 52 minutes today, quick agenda, recap the incident, what we've learned, immediate mitigations, and canary plan.
[00:12] Dana: yep, thanks, appreciate you fitting this in. timeline — spike around 13:40 our time, lots of 502/504 from the inference endpoint, hmm, roughly ~7% error rate across 30 minutes.
[00:25] Priya: got it, thank you. To confirm — these were from the batch job that sends sequences of varied length, is that right?
[00:31] Jamal: correct, the nightly summarization job, some inputs hit 4k tokens, others small. spikes correlated with longer sequences.
[00:40] Priya: ok, that's consistent with memory pressure on the GPU causing evictions and higher tail latency which then trips retries.
[00:48] Lena: we also saw client retries set to rapid retries: 100ms, 200ms, 400ms, three tries — I think those doubled our effective qps.
[00:56] Alex: classic thundering herd. When client retries are aggressive they end up amplifying transient server slowdowns into sustained errors.
[01:05] Jamal: yeah and in our logs two things — the Redwood endpoint returned 502 and then our client retried and got 500 a few times. sometimes back-to-back.
[01:15] Priya: small note — sometimes the transcript picks up 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated' so apologies if the auto text is funky.
[01:22] Alex: heh. ok. high level immediate mitigations? Priya, you wanna walk through?
[01:27] Priya: sure — 1) reduce client retry aggressiveness: set exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 2 for transient 5xx; 2) enable per-route prefix/KV cache for the summarization job to short-circuit frequent prefixes; 3) enable fallback routing: when latency > 1.5s or when error-rate exceeds threshold, route to a smaller quantized model variant; 4) increase telemetry sampling of failed requests including correlation ID.
[01:55] Marisol: fallback routing — what does that look like operationally? any change to our code?
[01:59] Priya: minimal — it's a routing policy on Redwood side. you tag the route with a fallback model id. SDK receives a 200 with a different model signature — client should be agnostic, but we recommend you validate outputs.
[02:12] Dana: are there quality regressions with a smaller model we should be worried about?
[02:16] Priya: yes there is, but for many summaries the smaller model is acceptable as a degraded mode. we can also quantize to int8 which drops cost/latency but may affect nuance. we'll provide a set of regression examples.
[02:27] Jamal: remote question — does fallback count against our quota differently?
[02:31] Alex: fallback uses the model you route to so billing aligns to that model rate. if you route to a cheaper quantized model you lower cost.
[02:38] Lena: about the rate limits — we saw 429s sporadically. are those token rate limits or concurrent inflight requests?
[02:43] Priya: Redwood has both per-token and concurrency caps; usually the 429s in your case were concurrency caps triggered by a brief burst. When clients retry they hold connections open longer so concurrency spikes.
[02:57] Jamal: interesting. so the fix might be both on client and server config.
[03:00] Priya: exactly. also adjust batching window — your job bundles variable lengths which forces larger batches under the hood. we recommend setting a max batch size and a shorter batch wait threshold for long-tail requests.
[03:12] Dana: ok can you show the specific settings you suggest?
[03:15] Priya: yes — I'll share a sample config: max_retries=2, base_backoff_ms=250, max_backoff_ms=2000, jitter=true; on server set concurrency_per_model=80 -> lower to 50 during peak testing. we'll attach to the email.
[03:31] Alex: also run a canary with 10% traffic, keep retention high for telemetry, and watch p95/p99 latency plus 5xxs.
[03:39] Marisol: timeline for that? Dana?
[03:41] Dana: we'll aim to start the canary on 14th, run 48 hours.
[03:45] Lena: when you run the canary, please turn on correlation IDs. we couldn't trace some of the failing requests last time since logs lacked the request id.
[03:53] Jamal: quick aside — we saw a couple of requests with long token lengths hitting GPU OOM and a 500 response, is that expected?
[03:59] Priya: sometimes long sequences cause out-of-memory on particular kernels. Redwood runtime has kernel selection logic but extreme sequences can still cause evictions; for those we recommend sequence length caps or automatic truncation with warning.
[04:13] Dana: hmm, auto-truncation might change our product output. can we instead fallback earlier?
[04:17] Priya: yes fallback before queueing the request is doable — route to a model that supports longer context or to the smaller model for faster response if latency is the main concern.
[04:27] Alex: another note — we want to avoid client-side retry loops that don't respect Retry-After. make sure your HTTP client honors headers.
[04:35] Jamal: our in-house client did not respect Retry-After well, good catch.
[04:39] Marisol: any blockers on Redwood side to enable prefix caching for us?
[04:43] Priya: no blockers, it's a config. we just need to know which endpoints to enable and expected prefix patterns. we'll provide recommended TTLs.
[04:52] Dana: about telemetry, what extra traces will Redwood provide in debug mode?
[04:56] Priya: we'll add full traces for failed requests, include kernel selection notes, batch composition, and GPU memory metrics. link will be shared to a gated dashboard.
[05:05] Alex: ok next — escalation path if the canary fails. Marco?
[05:09] Marco: yes, internal escalation — first level support (Marco) -> Priya (SE) -> Alex (AE) -> Eng on-call. We'll also open a high-priority ticket in the portal and attach logs. We'll share the escalation matrix doc after this call.
[05:21] Dana: perfect. any legal/compliance concerns with increased telemetry?
[05:25] Alex: we'll exclude PII, use correlation ids, and redact content per the DLP policy. Redwood can also run in your VPC if needed for sensitive data.
[05:35] Jamal: curious — has Redwood seen similar incidents with other customers? what patterns?
[05:40] Priya: yes, patterns usually are (1) aggressive client retries, (2) sequence-length spikes causing memory hot spots, (3) unexpected batch composition, (4) simultaneous model rollouts. Fixes are usually a mix of client backoff + fallback + cache.
[05:55] Dana: ok let's talk specifics of the test we'll run — metrics to monitor.
[05:58] Priya: monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate by status code, concurrency, GPU memory usage, and queue depth. Also track requests that hit fallback and quality regression samples.
[06:12] Marisol: can Redwood set an alert when fallback triggers exceed X%?
[06:15] Priya: yes we can set route-based alerts; default is 1% but we can tune.
[06:20] Alex: I'll summarise the plan: Redwood sends retry playbook + config, enable debug telemetry, Nimbus runs 10% canary 48h, share perf sheet, Redwood stands by to adjust model routing and concurrency.
[06:32] Jamal: sounds good. one more question — when should we consider Dedicated or private deployment? we were thinking about Dedicated if this keeps happening.
[06:40] Alex: Dedicated helps with isolation and predictable quotas but won't remove the need for retries/backoff or correct batching. It will lower noisy neighbor risk. Private/VPC helps with data residency but is a bigger lift.
[06:50] Dana: alright for now we'll stay hosted and follow the playbook. if we keep seeing memory pressure we'll re-evaluate Dedicated.
[06:57] Marisol: can you also share a short regression set to validate fallback outputs?
[07:00] Priya: yes we'll include a 20-sample regression set comparing the default model and fallback.
[07:06] Alex: ok any blockers on the acceptance criteria for the canary?
[07:10] Dana: acceptance — p95 < 1.2s, 5xx < 0.5% overall, and no quality regressions > 10% on sample set.
[07:21] Priya: noted, we'll aim for those.
[07:24] Lena: operational question — do we need to change rate limit windows in our client layer?
[07:29] Priya: you can implement a token-bucket at the client level to smooth bursts; this plus backoff should prevent concurrency spikes.
[07:36] Jamal: will Redwood adjust server-side auto-scaling during the canary?
[07:39] Priya: we can bump burst capacity and temporarily increase autoscale thresholds, but we prefer to test with realistic capacity to validate behavior. we'll coordinate.
[07:48] Alex: ok we'll capture these as action items. Marco will send escalation doc.
[07:52] Marco: will do.
[07:55] Dana: ok thanks everyone, one last ask — can you put the sample config in our shared drive rather than email?
[07:59] Alex: yes, we'll upload to the shared folder and post the link in the CRM ticket.
[08:04] Marisol: great. anything else?
[08:07] Lena: just please make sure headers show request id — we'll attach logs to the ticket.
[08:11] Priya: will do.
[08:13] Alex: thanks all. recap in the next steps, and we'll reconvene after the canary.
[08:18] Meeting end.
